points.t: Central facial redness, flushing and papules **without comedones** in an adult — or monomorphic pustules after steroids / long antibiotics.
Neurovascular and innate immune dysregulation (rosacea); drug or microbiome shifts driving folliculitis variants.
Rosacea: trigger avoidance, sunscreen, topical ivermectin (± oral doxycycline MR). Stop the culprit steroid or tetracycline when a mimic appears.
Rosacea fulminans (explosive central face in a young woman) and ocular keratitis — urgent ophthalmology / dermatology. Do not keep cycling antibiotics for Gram-negative folliculitis.

points: **Rosacea:** neurovascular dysregulation, innate immunity (cathelicidin), *Demodex*, UV; triggers include heat, alcohol, spicy food, hot drinks, topical steroids.
**Steroid acne / rosacea / perioral dermatitis:** oral, inhaled, topical or illicit bleaching steroids.
**Gram-negative folliculitis:** long-term oral tetracyclines for acne/rosacea → overgrowth of *Klebsiella*, *Enterobacter*, *Proteus*.
**Malassezia folliculitis:** yeast in oily follicles, often after antibiotics or steroids.
**Rosacea fulminans (pyoderma faciale):** explosive painful papules, pustules and nodules on a red swollen central face in young women; systemically well (unlike acne fulminans).
**Steroid acne:** sudden monomorphic papules/pustules on chest/back; few comedones.
**Perioral dermatitis:** papules around mouth with vermilion sparing; often after facial steroid.
**Gram-negative folliculitis:** new perinasal pustules after months of tetracycline that initially worked.
**Malassezia:** itchy monomorphic follicular pustules on chest/back.
**Hot-tub:** itchy pustules under the swimsuit line 1–4 days after spa use.

cards.clue: Systemically unwell young man; ulcerating trunk acne

items.t: Ocular pain, photophobia or reduced vision → same-day ophthalmology.
Rosacea fulminans or suspected acne fulminans → urgent dermatology.
Phyma needing procedural treatment; diagnostic doubt.
Acne worsening on long tetracyclines → culture for Gram-negatives; stop the antibiotic.

pearls.t: **No comedones + flushing + central face = rosacea until proven otherwise.**
Maintenance topical therapy is often needed — rosacea is relapsing.
Pharmacists often spot inhaled-steroid perioral dermatitis — advise rinsing/wiping the face after inhalers.
Laser/IPL for telangiectasia is usually private, not NHS-funded.
For the full rosacea ladder by phenotype, see [rosacea](condition:rosacea).
